Budget-Friendly Property in Washtenaw County, Michigan

Dive into property investment savings with Washtenaw County, Michigan’s tax foreclosure auctions, where discounts range between 40 to 90% off market values. Manage the auctions online through Auction.com, where early registration and thorough due diligence are required. Buyers purchase all properties in their current condition. The winning bid covers summer taxes, which the county pays directly to local treasurers upon payment.

Auction dates occur in July, August, and September. Bidders must register on Auction.com and commit to a $2,000 hold per asset, which they forfeit if they don’t complete the purchase. Failure to follow through can result in legal consequences and future auction bans.

Winners are notified via email and must submit specific documentation. Full payment is required within 48 hours, excluding credit or debit card transactions. Non-compliance may lead to legal action, including bids for specific performance and recovery of related legal costs.

Important Details for Washtenaw County Tax Sales

Washtenaw County Tax Deed Sale Information

The law mandates the sale of the tax-foreclosed property at public auction. Auctions are held on Auction.com. You must register for the auction on Auction.com prior to the first auction date to bid on the property.

I encourage bidders to complete all due diligence before participating in the auction. Helpful research sources may include local city/township assessors, treasurers, building departments, Washtenaw County Environmental Health, Water Resources, Road Commission, and Building Inspection. Check the BS&A Online municipal directory for some of this information.

Please read all Terms and Conditions carefully and thoroughly. Buyers purchase all properties as-is and where-is, releasing the Treasurer from any liability.

Conditions and Disclosures

Properties are sold “as-is” and “where is.” Buyers cover all 2023 property taxes, including state education, summer, winter, and/or village taxes, along with any accrued interest, fees, or special assessments. The initial bid includes 2023 summer taxes, which the Treasurer will pay to the local Treasurer upon receiving the winning bid payment.

Auction Participation

To participate, bidders must register on Auction.com, including a $2,000 hold on a credit card per asset bid on, forfeited if the winning bidder fails to complete the purchase. Bids are irrevocable and constitute a binding contract. Bidders agree not to sue the Treasurer, Washtenaw County, or related entities over auction processes.

Winning Bids

Winning bidders are notified by email with purchase details and payment instructions. Winners must complete a deed information form and an affidavit confirming no interest in properties with delinquent taxes or unpaid civil fines within Washtenaw County. Full payment is due within 48 hours of winning, excluding debit or credit card payments. Failure to pay will ban you from future sales and result in the forfeiture of your deposit.

Pro Tips

  • Thoroughly research each property before bidding.
  • Ensure funds are available to complete the purchase within the 48-hour window.
  • Understand the risks, including potential additional liens or environmental issues.

FAQs

How do I register for the auction?

  • Register on Auction.com and create an account before the auction date.

What happens if I win the bid but don’t pay?

  • Failure to comply results in forfeiting your $2,000 deposit, facing legal action, and a ban from future auctions.

Can I inspect the property before bidding?

  • Buyers purchase properties ‘as-is’ and often cannot inspect them before the auction.
